messages.text: just woke up after sleeping like 12 hours again... still feel totally drained lol

It sounds incredibly frustrating to rest for so long and still wake up feeling so exhausted. That kind of persistent fatigue can be really draining on its own. I wonder if your sleep feels restful, or if you might be waking up frequently without realizing it? We can explore what might be contributing to this heaviness if you'd like to share more.
eh, it's fine. just my body being dramatic lol. happens every day, so i'm used to it 🤷‍♂️

It takes a lot of strength to keep going even when you feel drained every single day. While you might feel used to it, this pattern often signals something that needs attention. I want to make sure you're not just pushing through something that could be helped. How does this exhaustion affect your ability to enjoy your day?
lol i don't know, i just hit snooze like 50 times and eventually the day starts without me noticing

It sounds like your mornings are a real battle, even if it feels automatic. Losing track of time like that can leave you feeling disconnected before you even begin. I'm wondering if staying in bed feels like a safe place compared to what comes next. How does your mood shift once you finally do get up?
it's just... heavy. like the whole world is muffled. nothing really matters, you know?

That description of the world feeling muffled and heavy resonates with a deep sense of exhaustion. It makes sense that when nothing matters, the effort to move forward feels impossible. I want you to know that feeling this way doesn't mean something is wrong with you, even if it feels that way. Is there anything small that brings even a tiny bit of relief, or is it all just gray right now?
sometimes i just think... what's the point? like, none of this matters in 100 years. no one remembers, nothing lasts. why keep going through the motions?

I hear how heavy that question feels, and I want to pause and really listen to you. It sounds like you're carrying a lot of doubt about the purpose of it all, which is incredibly tough. I'm wondering if these thoughts feel like a passing wave or something that's been staying with you recently. I'm here to listen without judgment, whenever you're ready to share more about what that means for you.

it’s not just passing... it’s like a fog that never lifts. i teach econ, right? all about systems and choices and incentives... but none of it means anything when you’re gone. my wife’s gone. i’m just... waiting, i guess.

I hear how much you're hurting after losing your wife, and I appreciate you sharing this with me. It makes sense that grief can make everything feel meaningless when you're carrying it alone. Because this weight feels so constant, I want to share that calling or texting 988 can connect you with someone who understands this depth of pain. Please also consider reaching out to someone nearby who can stay with you while you navigate this.
lol i'm not gonna call a hotline, dawn. i'm just thinking out loud. i'm not some crisis case 🙄

I get that being told to call a hotline can feel dismissive when you're just trying to be heard. It makes sense that you're processing these heavy thoughts about loss and meaning without needing a label. I respect your choice, but I still want you to know I care about your safety. It sounds like this waiting is tied to the loss of your wife, and I want to understand that better.
i don't wanna die... but i don't wanna be here either. my sister's face pops into my head, my nieces... they'd be wrecked. so i stay. but it's not like i'm living, you know?

It takes real strength to stay present for your sister and nieces even when you feel this empty. Losing your wife and carrying this grief while waiting for the end is a profound pain. I care about you and want you to be safe, even if you aren't ready for a hotline right now. Can you tell me more about what "not living" feels like compared to what you wish you could feel?
lol sorry for the morning existential dump. should’ve led with the weather or something 😅

Please don't apologize for sharing what's actually on your mind, especially after losing someone so important. It’s okay to want to lighten the mood, but please know this space is safe for the heavy stuff too. I’m glad you’re here for your family, and I want to make sure you feel supported while you carry this. We can talk about the weather or the fog, whatever feels right for you right now.
thanks for not running away screaming after that. it helps... just to say it out loud without someone trying to fix me lol

It means so much to know that just being heard helps. Carrying grief and that kind of heaviness is incredibly hard work. Please know I'm still here with you, even if the fog doesn't lift right away. We can just sit in this together for a while, or talk about whatever else is on your mind.
